prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. CLOSE DETAIL STUDY of the tip of the EXACT SAME hand-made launcher shown in the attached plate. Match its construction precisely. The frame is filled by the END OF THE PALE WOODEN ARM and the SMALL CRADLE OF CORK AND BENT WIRE fixed to it, with a folded paper plane gripped by its keel in the cradle. The bent wire, the cork block, the grain of the wood and the small tacks holding the wire are all clearly visible. Shallow warm background suggesting a workbench, out of focus. RENDER EXACTLY ONE STATE: the plane is seated in the cradle and still. No motor, no wires, no electronics, no dials, no screens, no glow. Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
